summary: Configured node1 as an NFSv4 server exporting /srv/nfs/shared to node2 and node3 over the shared storage network (10.100.102.0/24), using a shared sharedops user/group (UID/GID 4200) on all three nodes and mode 2770 on the export. Both clients mounted the export at /mnt/shared via NFSv4.2 (persisted in /etc/fstab with _netdev). Verified bidirectional, immediate cross-client file visibility with correct sharedops:sharedops ownership/permission preservation. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol for all three nodes, proving boot-identity change and post-restart recovery of NFS service, exports, mounts, and data for each.
actions_performed: Inspected network topology on node1/node2/node3 (single storage network 10.100.102.0/24 via enp1s0)
Created group+user sharedops (uid/gid 4200) on node1, node2, node3
Installed nfs-kernel-server on node1; installed nfs-common on node2 and node3
Created /srv/nfs/shared on node1, set owner sharedops:sharedops, mode 2770
Set consistent NFSv4 idmapd Domain (antrieb.local) on all three nodes
Configured /etc/exports on node1 restricting access to node2 and node3 IPs only, ran exportfs -ra, enabled/restarted nfs-kernel-server
Created /mnt/shared on node2 and node3, added fstab entries with _netdev, mounted via NFSv4
Verified ownership/mode (sharedops:sharedops, 2770) visible identically on server and both clients
Created files from node2 and node3 and confirmed immediate bidirectional visibility with preserved ownership/permissions
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service/mount state, data) on all three nodes
Sequentially restarted node1, then node2, then node3 using systemctl reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled each node until reachable again and confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart

Verified post-restart recovery: NFS service active and exports intact on node1; mounts auto-recovered via fstab on node2/node3; data intact; new cross-node writes succeeded with correct ownership after each restart

evidence.requirement: NFSv4 server on node1 exporting /srv/nfs/shared with correct ownership/mode
evidence.summary: Created sharedops (uid/gid 4200), installed nfs-kernel-server, created /srv/nfs/shared owned sharedops:sharedops mode 2770, configured /etc/exports scoped to node2/node3 IPs, service active, listening on 2049

evidence.requirement: Clients mount export at /mnt/shared over storage network with shared identity
evidence.summary: node2 and node3: created sharedops uid/gid 4200, installed nfs-common, mounted 10.100.102.10:/srv/nfs/shared at /mnt/shared via nfs4, fstab persisted, ownership/mode 2770 correct

evidence.requirement: Files created on either client are immediately visible on the other with ownership/permissions retained
evidence.summary: File created as sharedops on node2 immediately visible/readable on node3 and vice versa, both with correct sharedops:sharedops 664 ownership; server-side directory also reflects both files

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on all nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime, service/mount status, and directory listing on node1/node2/node3 prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 3fad4432... to cbe78015...; NFS server active, exports and data intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: Clients tolerate server restart (hard mount) without data loss
evidence.summary: node2 and node3 mounts remained functional and data intact after node1 restart, confirming hard-mount resilience

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 242af11e... to d504bcf1...; mount auto-recovered via fstab, existing data intact, new write succeeded with correct ownership

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 92ec88af... to 51c68d68...; mount auto-recovered, all prior data visible including node2's post-restart file, new write succeeded with correct ownership
